key_insight: Recurrent quantum reinforcement learning improves tracking of time-varying Hamiltonians while retaining accurate identification under stationary dynamics.
engineering_relevance: Adaptive Hamiltonian estimation could support quantum-device calibration and monitoring when system parameters drift or operating regimes change.
method: Formulate Hamiltonian identification as reinforcement learning from sequential quantum-state observations.
Use Vanilla-QRL for stationary dynamics and recurrent GRU-QRL for non-stationary tracking.
Compare against a Quantum Graph Recurrent Neural Network baseline.
evidence_signal: Evaluations on transverse-field Ising systems cover stationary dynamics, abrupt and rapid switching, randomized switch locations, gradual drift, and frozen-policy tests on unseen trajectories.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish robustness to hardware noise or the measurement and computational costs of deployment.
paper_title: Adaptive Hamiltonian Identification via Quantum Reinforcement Learning under Non-Stationary Dynamics
